WWE Unreal Season 3 Is Coming: Cast, Release Date, Episodes, and What to Know

Go behind the scenes as John Cena says goodbye.

By Christopher Hudspeth

June 23, 2026

WWE Unreal is making its return with a fresh batch of behind-the-scenes action in Season 3.

After taking fans deeper than ever inside World Wrestling Entertainment’s creative process, the hit docuseries will once again pull back the curtain on some of the biggest moments, boldest decisions, and unforgettable storytelling with some of the WWE’s greatest legends who’ve shaped the industry and new stars who are emerging as prominent parts of the future.

What will be shown in WWE Unreal Season 3?

In WWE Unreal Season 3, John Cena says goodbye, a fan favorite returns, and the next generation of Superstars rise to the occasion.

The series takes viewers inside the writers room as injuries, last-minute pivots, and career-defining decisions reshape WWE’s biggest season yet heading into WrestleMania 42.

Who will be featured in WWE Unreal Season 3?

The cast of WWE Superstars featured in WWE Unreal Season 3 includes John Cena, Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, CM Punk, AJ Lee, Trick Williams, Lash Legend, Stephanie Vaquer, Oba Femi, Bron Breakker, Chelsea Green, Matt Cardona, Seth Rollins, and Becky Lynch.

When does WWE Unreal Season 3 come out?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will be released on July 21.

How many episodes are in WWE Unreal Season 3?

WWE Unreal Season 3 will have five 50-minute episodes.

Strap in and prepare to be a fly on the wall backstage during some of the WWE’s most riveting moments. (Netflix)

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

WWE Unreal

WWE Unreal is a professional wrestling documentary and reality series on Netflix that provides an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the creative process and internal operations of WWE.

WWE Unreal

Show Overview

Genre: Reality television / Documentary series.

Premise: The series follows WWE Superstars and executives, notably Paul "Triple H" Levesque, as they plan storylines in the writers' room and manage the "Gorilla Position" during live broadcasts.

Production: A collaboration between WWE, Omaha Productions (Peyton Manning), NFL Films, and Skydance Sports.

Here's the latest Netflix news as of mid-January 2026!

The streaming giant is kicking off the year strong with a packed slate of new releases, ongoing buzz around major deals, and continued subscriber growth.

Major Highlights

Netflix is reportedly in the midst of a blockbuster acquisition: the company has agreed to buy Warner Bros. in a massive deal valued at around $82.7 billion (with some reports citing $72 billion in equity value).

This move aims to supercharge its content library with iconic franchises like Harry Potter and classic films.

However, there's drama — Paramount Skydance has launched a competing hostile takeover bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, adding some high-stakes industry intrigue!

Netflix ended 2025 with over 301.6 million global subscribers, solidifying its position as the top streaming platform.

What's New & Coming in January 2026

January is loaded with fresh originals, from thrilling mysteries to romantic adaptations and long-awaited returns.

Here are some of the standout releases that are lighting up the charts and generating buzz right now:

People We Meet on Vacation — A charming rom-com adaptation of the Emily Henry novel, starring Emily Bader — it's been topping the charts as one of the biggest new movies of the year so far!

The Rip — This high-octane action-thriller directed by Joe Carnahan reunites Ben Affleck and Matt Damon — it's one of the most anticipated films dropping mid-month, perfect for fans of intense heist vibes!

His & Hers — A gripping mystery series starring Tessa Thompson and Jon Bernthal, following estranged spouses racing to solve a murder. It's been climbing the Top 10 with strong buzz around its twists.

💢General Atomics Reaper’ın halefini “Wildfire” İHA’sını tanıttı:

🇺🇸ABD’nin önde gelen savunma sanayi şirketi General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI), ABD Hava Kuvvetleri’nin MQ-9A Reaper insansız hava araçlarının yerini alması amacıyla başlattığı ihale kapsamında yeni platformu “Wildfire”ı tanıttı.

🔬Savunma İnovasyon Birimi (DIU) tarafından yürütülen Kütlesel Modüler Hava Aracı (Massed Modular Aircraft - MMA) programına sunulan Wildfire, maliyet etkinliği, yüksek üretim kapasitesi ve uzun menzil yetenekleriyle öne çıkıyor.

✈️General Atomics tarafından yapılan açıklamaya göre Wildfire, 8 bin deniz milini (yaklaşık 14 bin 800 kilometre) aşan intikal menziline ve en az 1.270 kilogram (2.800 libre) faydalı yük taşıma kapasitesine sahip.

🎯Derin darbe ve taarruz görevleri için tasarlanan platform, aynı anda iki adet AGM-158C LRASM (Uzun Menzilli Gemi Karşıtı Füze) veya dört adet JSM (Müşterek Taarruz Füzesi) taşıma imkanı sunuyor. İHA ayrıca çeşitli sensörler, sürü harekatı mühimmatları ve elektronik harp sistemleriyle de donatılabiliyor.

General Atomics offers a solution with a 14,800 km range

🇺🇸General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. (GA-ASI) has unveiled its new "Wildfire" uncrewed aircraft system as part of a U.S. Air Force tender aimed at replacing the service's fleet of MQ-9A Reaper drones.

🔬The platform was submitted for the Massed Modular Aircraft (MMA) program—managed by the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)—and is designed to emphasize cost efficiency, high-volume production, and extended operational range.

✈️According to a company statement, Wildfire features a ferry range exceeding 8,000 nautical miles (approximately 14,800 kilometers) and a payload capacity of at least 2,800 pounds (1,270 kilograms).

🎯Engineered for deep-strike and attack missions, the platform can carry two AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missiles (LRASMs) or four Joint Strike Missiles (JSMs) simultaneously. The aircraft can also be configured with a variety of sensors, air-launched effectors for swarm operations, and electronic warfare suites.

This is something that basically every person working on games experiences on a near daily basis.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On a Wednesday evening in September 1899, at the corner of West 74th Street and Central Park West, a sixty-nine-year-old real estate man named Henry Hale Bliss stepped down from a southbound Eighth Avenue trolley. He turned, as a gentleman would, to offer his hand to a companion known to us only as Miss Lee. It was an ordinary courtesy on an ordinary night in a city still largely moved by horses and steel rails.

What came next was not ordinary.

An electric taxicab—Automobile Number 43, driven by a man named Arthur Smith—swerved to avoid a truck that blocked the curb. Two wheels passed over Henry Bliss. His skull and chest were crushed. A physician riding in the cab, Dr. David Orr Edson, son of a former mayor of New York, did what he could until the ambulance came. At Roosevelt Hospital the house surgeon looked at the injuries and knew at once there was no hope. Henry Hale Bliss died the next morning, September 14, 1899. He was the first person in the United States known to have been killed by an automobile.

There were then perhaps twenty-five hundred automobiles in the entire country. They were still novelties, many of them electric, quiet as ghosts compared with the clatter of hooves. The stretch of avenue where Bliss fell already had a name among the trolley motormen: Dangerous Stretch. Newspapers far from New York printed the story. One of them wrote, with a kind of grim poetry, that the automobile had “tasted blood.”

Arthur Smith was arrested and charged with manslaughter. He said the truck had forced him closer to the trolley than he wished to be. The court found neither malice nor negligence and let him go. The law had not yet learned how to speak of such machines.

A hundred years later a plaque was set in the sidewalk at that same corner. Bliss’s great-granddaughter laid flowers there. The city remembered a man who had only meant to help someone off a streetcar.

We look back now and see the beginning of something vast—the remaking of American streets, of American life itself. But on that September evening it was simply a man named Henry Bliss, going home, offering his hand, and never reaching the other side of the street.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the thirteenth of September, 1788, in the fading light of the old Confederation Congress, a resolution was passed that would change the course of the country. The men assembled that day were not the celebrated figures of Philadelphia two summers earlier. They were the last remnant of a government that had already outlived its usefulness—tired, underfunded, and all too aware that the Constitution they had helped bring into being was about to render them obsolete. Yet they did their duty. They set the date for the first presidential election under the new frame of government and named New York City the temporary capital of the United States.

It was a quiet act, almost bureaucratic on the surface. Electors were to be chosen the first Wednesday in January 1789; those electors would cast their ballots the first Wednesday in February. Everyone in the room understood what the result would be. George Washington, the man who had already given the country eight years of his life and then gone home to Mount Vernon, would be called back once more.

What those congressmen understood, and what we sometimes forget, is how fragile the whole enterprise still felt. The Articles of Confederation had produced a government that could neither pay its debts nor command respect abroad. Thirteen states pulled in thirteen directions. The Constitution had been ratified, but a constitution is only words until it is given a face and a place. That September they supplied both.

They chose New York not by accident. It was the great commercial city of the young nation, a port that looked out upon the world rather than inward upon itself. Philadelphia had been the scene of so much already—the Declaration, the Convention, the long years of war. New York offered a fresh start and the practical advantages of a thriving harbor and a growing financial community. By placing the new government there, they signaled that this republic would be a trading nation, a nation of enterprise as well as of farms and forests.

And they chose Washington because no other choice was possible. He had refused a crown when it was offered. He had laid down his sword at Annapolis and gone home. That very refusal made him indispensable. The office of the presidency was being created around the one man the country already trusted to occupy it. His election would not look like a grab for power. It would look like the natural, almost inevitable, next step in a story that had begun at Lexington and Concord.

One can imagine the scene: the modest chamber, the late-summer heat, the sense among the members that they were closing one chapter and opening another they would not live to see completed. They were, in their way, like the last keepers of an old house preparing it for new occupants. They set the calendar. They named the city. Then they stepped aside.

From that resolution came everything that followed—the inauguration on the balcony of Federal Hall the next April, the first Cabinet, the long, difficult work of turning a paper government into a living one. It is easy, from this distance, to take it all for granted. It was not granted. It was decided, carefully and deliberately, on a September day in 1788 by men who knew the experiment could still fail.

America 250 🇺🇸

1. Jordan Love O20.5 completions — CGS 9.1

This is the strongest passing position on the rebuilt board.

Our frozen expectation lands at 23.4 completions. The current market is 20.5, and Action's Sunday update also lists the Over at -102; its independent model projects nearly 25 completions and a 72% chance of 21+.

The key is Best Expression. I do not prefer Love's passing-yard Over. Minnesota allowed only 172.3 passing yards per game last season and generated considerable pressure; a lower-aDOT, completion-heavy game can therefore support Over completions while still making the yardage market much less attractive.

Model hit: 67%
 Break-even: 50.5%
 Estimated EV: +32.7%
That separation is why Love sits alone above 9.0.
2. Jacoby Brissett U22.5 completions — CGS 8.7

Brissett's blind volume projection lands around 19.3 completions against the Chargers.

The current market is U22.5 -124. FTN independently projects only 18.1 completions and identifies the Chargers as a difficult passing matchup after allowing just 179.9 passing yards per game in 2025.

Current market data also has Brissett at 22.5 completions, confirming that the number hasn't moved far enough to erase the edge.

The Cardinals may chase points, but more attempts don't necessarily translate into enough completions against this defense.

3. Baker Mayfield O229.5 yards — CGS 8.6

Mayfield's frozen projection comes in at 244 passing yards.

Action's fresh Sunday board has O229.5 -115, and its separate projection also lands at 244 yards. Cincinnati allowed 245.1 passing yards per game to quarterbacks last season, while the current game environment remains one of Sunday's stronger potential passing environments.

Tampa no longer has Mike Evans, but the likely scoring pressure from Cincinnati supports pass volume, and Baker still has enough receiving talent to push the number.

Model separation: +14.5 yards
 Model hit: 62%
 Estimated EV: +15.9%

4. Cooper Rush U18.5 completions — CGS 8.3

Rush is a more volatile position, which is why his CGS stays below the top three.
Atlanta is starting him because Tua Tagovailoa is out, and Rush is also dealing with back spasms, although Atlanta still expects him to start.
The current market is U18.5 completions -120. Action's current analysis puts his likely output closer to 17.5 completions and expects Atlanta to shift toward a more run-heavy game plan behind Bijan Robinson.

Our frozen number is 16.8 completions.

There is obvious tail risk if Atlanta falls behind and throws heavily, but Rush's physical uncertainty and potential for Atlanta to protect him support the Under.

5. Daniel Jones O21.5 completions — CGS 8.2

Jones returns from his Achilles injury, which reduces Projection Confidence but also creates an interesting stylistic angle.

Our expectation is approximately 22.9 completions. Current pricing has O21.5 -118, matching the number identified by Action.

Jones may scramble less early in the season and operate more through quick throws to Josh Downs, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen. Action's independent model also puts him near 22.5 completions with roughly a 60% chance of clearing 21.5.

The edge is real, but Achilles-return uncertainty keeps this at 8.2, not 8.7+.

Major name that did NOT survive: Lamar Jackson

Lamar is a good example of why the final scan matters.

Earlier markets offered 27.5 or 28.5 pass attempts, where an Under case existed. But the current board has compressed toward approximately 26.5 attempts, dramatically reducing the available edge.

Action still shows U28.5 -135, noting that Baltimore has averaged fewer than 26 attempts per game since Derrick Henry arrived.

At 28.5, I'd like the Under. At 26.5, I don't have enough separation for an Official CGS play.

PASS — price/line dependent.

text:
Podcast Summary | This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von: #682 - Bishop Robert Barron

Overview
Bishop Robert Barron reframes the biggest questions of existence around a single claim: God is not one being among many but the uncaused cause and ground of all being, so evil, suffering, love, grace, and even technology only make sense in that light. The conversation moves from God as the answer to why anything exists at all, to evil as a lack of being, to the human vocation of love and reconciliation, to what is lost when initiation, storytelling, and spiritual discipline disappear. Barron argues that modern people are materially saturated but spiritually lost, that sin works like addiction, and that the church must recover boldness rather than accommodate culture. The thread tying it together: people would rather be ruined than changed, yet transformation comes through grace, prayer, and the willingness to let illusions die.

Key Themes
- God is the ground of being rather than a rival being, which reframes the question of why there is something rather than nothing.
- Evil is a lack of being, not a created thing, so God permits it toward a greater good while remaining the cause of all being.
- Love is willing the good of the other as other, and it breaks the ego's gravitational pull toward self-regard.
- Grace is a free gift starting with existence itself, and the theological virtues cannot be attained by practice alone.
- Sin operates like addiction, and putting anything other than God at the center leads to insatiability and captivity.
- Christianity affirms the body and the material world, pointing to bodily resurrection and a new heavens and new earth rather than escape from earth.
- The modern culture of self-invention produces misery, while objective values in art, music, and morality can reorient a life.
- Initiation, storytelling, and apprenticeship have eroded, leaving many people uninitiated and stuck in self-regard.
- The church is called to be salt, light, and ambassadors of reconciliation, not merely private believers.

Detailed Summary
Barron frames God as the uncaused cause and ground of being, not a being alongside other things. The answer to why there is something rather than nothing is God. On evil and suffering, evil is described as a lack of being rather than a created thing. God is the cause of all being but permits evil, and the Book of Job is cited as the best biblical wrestling with why God permits suffering. Barron compares evil to a cavity in a tooth: real and painful, but an emptiness rather than a positive thing. He references Tolkien's Nazgul, fearsome figures whose cloaks fall away to reveal nothing, illustrating evil as a type of non-being.

Becoming a bishop is presented as an unexpected appointment by the pope, with no prior warning to the person under consideration. Refusal is possible only with a very strong reason. Barron is bishop of the Diocese of Winona-Rochester in southern Minnesota and lives in Rochester near the Mayo Clinic, where he visits many sick people. His first appointment was as auxiliary bishop of Los Angeles, received unexpectedly on a Sunday afternoon while watching golf. He later received another call appointing him to Winona-Rochester. Before priesthood he worked at a bookstore as a stock boy at sixteen and briefly as a dishwasher at Steak and Shake, which he disliked. He became a priest around age twenty-six.

Word on Fire is described as a media and evangelical ministry begun twenty-five years ago as a radio sermon show in Chicago, now spanning publishing, podcasting, and films. Catholicism is explained as a branch of Christianity claiming to be the true church founded by Jesus Christ and possessing the fullness of what Christ wanted, while acknowledging gifts in Protestant churches. Thomas Merton's The Seven Storey Mountain is presented as a major personal influence on Barron at sixteen, modeling a human story of falling in love with God. Merton died in 1968 in Bangkok by electrocution after a fan apparently fell on him or he grabbed it. Barron describes Merton as a talented New York writer who became Catholic and then a Trappist monk, and as one of the great spiritual writers of the last century.

Building a relationship with God starts with dedicating time daily, through practices like a holy hour, prayer, rosary, or silent meditation. Merton advised taking the time in response to how to start. Fulton Sheen popularized the holy hour, an hour in front of the Blessed Sacrament, and is described as a mid-twentieth-century teacher and early user of radio and television, about to be beatified. Beatification is the last step before canonization. Mental prayer and the rosary are described as ways to calm and focus the soul. Honesty with God is emphasized because God already knows everything, and hiding things is pointless and tied to the father of lies. Confession is praised as psychologically healthy, with Jordan Peterson quoted saying admitting failure before a representative of God and seeking grace is healthy.

Existence itself is framed as grace, a free gift, since there is nothing necessary about our being. God is perfect and needs nothing outside himself, so creation is not from need but from pure love. Aquinas defines love as willing the good of the other as other, not transactional kindness done for reciprocation. Most people, described as sinners, operate transactionally: kind if treated kindly, hostile if treated badly. Maximilian Kolbe is cited as an example, a Franciscan friar imprisoned at Auschwitz who volunteered to take the place of a man selected to be starved to death. The starvation was a Nazi reprisal after an escape, with ten prisoners selected at random. Kolbe barely knew the man and identified himself as a Catholic priest.

Theological virtues of faith, hope, and love are distinguished from virtues like courage, prudence, and justice, because they cannot be attained by practice alone and require God's grace. Prayer is presented as necessary for becoming selfless, and the desire to please God is said to itself please God. Merton's prayer is cited, including the line that the desire to please God does in fact please God. Paul is quoted from Romans 7: the good I would do, I do not do. Prayer for willingness is described as a possible crack in the door when one lacks power to act.

Evil operates on multiple levels: personal sin, institutional and structural sin, and a fallen spiritual dimension behind both. The Bible affirms the material world and the body rather than treating them as things to escape. The goal is a new heavens and new earth, not escape from earth. Resurrection is bodily: Jesus ate and showed his wounds, and the creeds point to resurrection of the body. The human body is portrayed as continuously reconstituted in nature, and the resurrected body is analogized as God remembering and reconstituting the pattern of a person in a transfigured form. Being alone is framed as not good, and connection between people is grounded in God as familial and communitarian.

Christians are called to be reconcilers and ambassadors of Christ, and failure to do this contributes to divided societies. The Amish response to a school shooting is presented as radical grace: community members comforted the killer's widow and showed support at his trial. The modern culture of self-invention, deciding one's own values and autonomy, is described as a recipe for disaster and depression. Great objective values in art, music, and morality draw people out of themselves and can reorient their lives. Technology and social media are described as tools of dark powers, especially damaging young people and young women through meanness, negativity, and judgmentalism. The appropriate response to great value is aesthetic arrest: stopping, letting the thing judge you, being reworked, and then going on mission.

The loss of in-person storytelling and apprenticeship means a real but unquantified loss of human connection in transmitting stories, skills, mindsets, and beliefs. Machines can supply data but cannot supply pattern and meaning, which come through community, lore, and narrativity. Initiation rituals across primal cultures followed a pattern: extraction from comfort, bodily marking, transmission of tribal lore, and a survival ordeal ending with return to the tribe. A modern concern is that many people are uninitiated, stuck in self-regard, and not brought through a process that makes them useful to the community. Religion historically presided over initiation, and without the church acting with confidence and purpose, it is unclear what institution fills that role. The gates of hell will not prevail is reframed: the church is not merely defending against hell but on the offensive against the powers of darkness.

The church is criticized for lacking boldness and accommodating to culture. Humility is described as the one thing the devil cannot manipulate, because it is contrary to pride and self-regard. True humility is framed as a position of power, letting go of ego so God can work through a person. Sin is framed as addiction: putting anything other than God at the center leads to insatiability and captivity. Self-consciousness and misery are linked, while joy comes from being drawn out of oneself through love. The Little Way of St. Therese is summarized as finding the path of love in every moment. A high school religion teacher demonstrated influence by putting one drop of blue dye into a glass of water; by the end of class the water was entirely blue.

Fear is presented as something that can be detached from through spiritual practice, with the Buddhist invite your fears in for tea exercise translated into Christian terms as detachment spirituality. Spiritual maturity is framed as being detached from both success and failure and from the goods of the world, which produces freedom. The speaker claims God can only work with free people, sinners are described as addicts, and religion is described as a kind of treatment program for addiction. Pornography is discussed as a major societal and spiritual problem, especially for young people, with claims that it harms brain chemistry, distorts how men view women, and damages marital connection. The cross is presented as powerful because Jesus on the cross embodies the stripping away of all wealth, pleasure, power, honor, and fear while remaining ordered to God.

The central theme is that people would rather be ruined than changed, preferring comfort in hypothetical alternatives over risk and transformation. Evil and suffering can be reframed as God stripping away addictions and illusions. Jesus' call to metanoia means going beyond the mind you have, challenging an addictive, self-regarding, self-protecting mindset. Religion is framed as being about joy and full life, not misery. Shame can be healthy when felt in the presence of God, and conscience is described as Christ's voice in the soul. Indulgences are explained as calling on the treasury of Christ's self-sacrifice and became abusive when bought and sold, especially around the Reformation.

The modern political state of Israel is distinguished from biblical Israel. The church recognizes Israel's right to exist and opposes anti-Semitism, while Catholics may criticize government policies. On clergy sexual abuse, the claim is that predators may seek authority and access to young people, and that abuse is not unique to the celibate priesthood but also occurs in families, schools, and other youth organizations. The claim that celibate priesthood causes attraction to children is rejected as demonstrably false. A more plausible explanation offered is that people attracted to children may deliberately seek positions of authority and access to children.

The Church is described as having responded strongly to the abuse crisis through seminary screening, psychological testing, ongoing education programs, zero tolerance, removal from priesthood, and reporting accusations to secular authorities. A past institutional failure is acknowledged, in which bishops sometimes sent accused priests for prayer or treatment and reassigned them, an approach now rejected. Concerns are raised that AI and data dependency could erode human understanding, replace prayer and relationship, function as a new god, threaten jobs tied to human dignity, and enable surveillance and manipulation. The Pope is portrayed as neither anti-AI nor uncritical: AI should remain a human-controlled tool judged by whether it protects human dignity, work, freedom, truth, and the vulnerable. The Tower of Babel is used as a biblical symbol of technological overreach turning on itself and undermining itself.

text:
Maintenance is the #1 activity we spend time on in our yards, but creating a more natural landscape can mean less work for you and more benefits for pollinators, wildlife, and the environment.

There are many reasons to embrace the use of Missouri’s wonderful native plants. They create beauty and interest with a progression of flowers and fruits, and they furnish food and cover for butterflies, birds and other wildlife. 

In addition, they:
• Are adapted to our climate.
• Are adapted to our soils.
• Require little or no irrigation.
• Seldom require fertilizer or pesticides.
• The current mix of Missouri native plants has been here since the last Ice Age, about 10,000 years ago.
• Native plants evolved with Missouri’s geology, climate and wildlife.
• Many wildlife species prefer native plants for habitat and depend on them for survival.
• Well-established and maintained native-plant communities help resist invasive
non-natives that threaten wildlife habitat and crops.
• Native plants help preserve our natural diversity.

Where to Buy Native Plants this Spring - Here in Mid-Missouri, we are fortunate to have multiple nurseries that offer native plants.The following are a few options: 

Sunrise Gardens 
Established in 2011, Sunrise Gardens is a local nursery dedicated to wildlife gardens and sustainable landscapes. Find them every Saturday at the Columbia Farmers Market, or order online from their website for nursery pickup! 
https://t.co/H69dfwX2hW 

Missouri Wildflower Nursery 
Located in Jefferson City, Missouri Wildflower Nursery offers a wide variety of native plants seed and transplants. If you’re looking to cultivate a tidy garden, use their “formal landscape filter” and select plants rated three or four stars! 
https://t.co/aUBbJtIZHk 

Superior Garden Center 
Superior Garden Center can be found off the Midway exit west of Columbia. Search “Missouri Native” in their plant inventory to identify native options for your garden. As a part of Rost Inc. they also offer landscaping services that utilize native plants. 
https://t.co/jTk2UduwNC

CMSE Giving Gardens 
For over 50 years, CMSE’s goal has been to offer meaningful work to people with disabilities. They offer a variety of plants, including some native perennials. You can find them off of S. Bearfield Rd. 
https://t.co/hrCu3XCziu

text:
The date on of that video is very interesting...1962.  Because it was in that year that he started buying shares in a New England textile company. By 1965, Buffett had acquired 7% of this textile company.  

This company's CEO implemented a very flawed strategy of using share buybacks to try to clean up a failing balance sheet.

When unprofitable mills were shuttered, the CEO was using the proceeds from the liquidation of those mills to buy back shares.

In 1965, he went to Buffett, as the largest shareholder, to solicit his shares.  Buffet named his price...11.50 per share.  The CEO agreed (or, so says Buffett), but when the official tender offer arrived, the quoted price for the shares was 11.385 per share....1/8 of a point lower than agreed upon.

Buffett got very mad at this, and, out of spite (literally), he decided that instead of selling, he would make a hostile offer for the entire company....so he could fire the CEO.

I'm sure everyone has guessed the name of this New England textile company.  Berkshire Hathaway.

Fun fact...Buffett has called this decision to buy Berkshire Hathaway "the worst decision of his life."  And, not as a joke, either.

The reason is, Buffett didn't immediately turn it into the holding company it has now become.  He actually tried to keep the textile company alive for the next 20 years, while also using it as a holding company.  

It wasn't until 1985 until the textile part of the business was shut down.  Buffett has said he spent tens of millions to keep it going....money that could have been invested in other businesses.  

At the time of his Berkshire purchase, Buffett said he had just figured out the cash cow that could be created by buying insurance companies and investing the float of those insurance companies. 

He was actually working on buying an insurance company to do just that....National Indemnity, in Omaha, Nebraska.

If he didn't decide to buy Berkshire, he would have bought National Indemnity directly, and that would have become his holding company....without a textile business siphoning tens of millions of dollars for two decades.

Buffett has said that if he had skipped Berkshire and just bought National Indemnity directly, the company would be worth probably twice what Berkshire is worth, today.  He did end up buying National Indemnity....through Berkshire.  It was the first company bought by Berkshire.

Nov 16

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

Nov 16

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

Rather than small, winged sprites or giant, cave-dwelling lizards guarding hoards of gold, these beings possess highly unique, humanoid, and elemental traits.  The Hungarian Dragon (Sárkány)In Hungarian folktales, a dragon is rarely just a wild, fire-breathing beast. Instead, it is a cunning, magical opponent that represents a hero's internal flaws or a test of adulthood. The Evolution: According to legend, a sárkány isn't born a dragon. Instead, a fish or a snake that lives hidden in a swamp for seven straight years transforms into a dragon. Human-like Behavior: Unlike Western dragons, the Hungarian sárkány is often man-shaped. They wear clothes, ride horses, live in castles, wield weapons, and are even known to sing, dance, and drink wine. Weather Masters: They are heavily tied to nature and act as demons of bad weather. They control storms, blizzards, and thunderclouds, and they are said to literally "eat the sun" during eclipses. Multiples of Three: They always have multiple heads, usually in multiples of three or seven—such as 6, 9, 12, or 24 heads. In battles, the hero must slice off every single head to truly defeat them.  The Hungarian Fairy (Tündér)The tündér (plural: tündérek) are closer in appearance to the majestic, human-sized Elves of modern fantasy than to tiny pixies. Radiant and Human-Sized: They appear as breathtakingly beautiful, young, eternal women. They are so human-like that they frequently fall in love and marry mortal men. Tied to Water: They are deeply connected to nature's waterways. The most famous fairy legends originate from the riverlands of northwestern Hungary, where fairies are said to build magnificent underwater crystal palaces and domes. The Origin of Gold: Hungarian folklore uses fairies to explain why gold is found in rivers. One popular myth says that when the fairies comb their long, golden hair, the loose strands fall into the water and turn into gold dust. Another sweet myth claims that when a tündér cries, her tears instantly transform into pearls that she leaves behind for orphans and the poor. Fickle Nature: While they often act as magical benefactors who grant three wishes to heroes, they are not purely good. Hungarian Mushroom Cream Pizza — sour‑cream mushroom ragout as the sauce base.  Brokkoli–Paprika Garden Pizza — based on Hungarian veggie pizza traditions.  Fruitarian Hungarian cuisine isn’t fruitarian by tradition, but you can reinterpret its sweet paprika warmth and forest‑fruit heritage:  Paprika‑Apricot Raw Pizza — dehydrated apple‑flax crust, apricot purée, sweet paprika, sliced peppers (raw).  Forest Berry–Pepper Mosaic — figs, grapes, mulberries, raw peppers, lemon, cold‑pressed olive oil.  Raw Tomato–Paprika Tart — tomato‑paprika jelly set with citrus pectin.  Hungarian Halloween recipes — especially in a gothic‑era, night‑ritual, folklore‑heavy style — draw from three deep wells of tradition:  Medieval Magyar harvest foods (pumpkin, cabbage, apples, poppy seed, rye).  Fire‑spirit folklore from pre‑Christian and early Christian Germania/Hungary.  All Souls’ Night customs (halottak napja), where food was left for wandering spirits.  Below is a full set of gothic Hungarian Halloween recipes, written in the mythic, symbolic, astral‑gothic tone you prefer — each beginning with a Guided Link so you can open whichever path you want next.  Gothic Hungarian Halloween Recipes Hungarian autumn food is already halfway to Halloween: smoky paprika, black breads, poppy seeds, ember‑colored stews, and orchard fruits that glow like lanterns. These recipes reinterpret them through a gothic‑era lens — medieval, folkloric, fire‑lit.  Ember‑Witch Pumpkin Paprikás  Ember‑Witch Paprikás A Halloween reinterpretation of pumpkin paprikás, imagined as something cooked in a cauldron beside a village fire‑altar.  Pumpkin simmered with smoked paprika, garlic, and bay.  Add mushrooms for depth.  Finish with oat cream for a vegan version.  Serve in black bowls with rye bread. Vegan / vegetarian.  Black Poppy‑Seed Moonbread  Moonbread Hungarian poppy seed (mák) becomes a gothic midnight bread.  Dark rye dough enriched with ground poppy seed.  Add molasses for a near‑black color.  Shape into crescent moons for Halloween. Vegan.  Symbolically: poppy is the seed of sleep, dreams, and the underworld — perfect for a gothic feast.  Night‑Forest Apple & Caraway Stew  Night‑Forest Stew Inspired by medieval orchard offerings left for wandering spirits.  Apples stewed with cabbage, caraway, and black pepper.  Add walnuts and a splash of vinegar.  Serve warm at night with candles. Vegan.  Fire‑Spirit Csárda Pot  Fire‑Spirit Csárda Pot A Halloween version of Hungarian goulash, built around fire symbolism.  Potatoes, peppers, onions, paprika, and smoked salt.  Add mushrooms instead of meat.  Simmer until the broth turns ember‑red. Vegan / vegetarian.  This dish echoes ancient fire‑guardian spirits (tűz‑szellemek) believed to protect hearths during autumn storms.  Witch‑Queen Honey‑Pumpkin Tart (Vegetarian)  Witch‑Queen Tart A gothic‑era reinterpretation of medieval pumpkin sweets.  Pumpkin purée mixed with honey, cinnamon, and clove.  Bake in a barley‑almond crust.  Decorate with black poppy seeds. Vegetarian; vegan with maple instead of honey.  Carpathian Shadow‑Cabbage  Shadow‑Cabbage A charred cabbage dish inspired by Carpathian mountain folklore.  Cabbage wedges roasted until nearly black.  Drizzle with juniper oil and black vinegar.  Serve with barley bread. Vegan.  Fruitarian: Blood‑Moon Apple & Paprika Mosaic  Blood‑Moon Mosaic A fruitarian reinterpretation of Hungarian paprika warmth.  Thin‑sliced apples arranged in a spiral.  Dust with sweet paprika and lemon.  Add raw peppers, figs, and grapes.  Drizzle with cold‑pressed olive oil. Fruitarian.  🕯 Gothic‑Era Context Hungarian Halloween isn’t medieval in origin, but All Souls’ Night and harvest fire rites were. Medieval Magyar villages lit guardian fires to protect homes from spirits and storms. Food was often:  left at crossroads,  placed on windowsills,  or eaten beside communal bonfires.  These recipes echo that world: smoky, ember‑colored, orchard‑sweet, poppy‑dark. Fire‑spirit food lore belongs to the old cosmology of flame — the world where every ember had a name, every hearth had a guardian, and every pot simmering at night was an offering to something watching from the dark. Below is a full mythic system of Hungarian–Germania fire‑spirits expressed through culinary rites, seasonal dishes, and ritual foods. Each spirit begins with a Guided Link so you can open whichever path you want next.  Fire‑Spirit Food Lore of the Old Magyar Night In gothic‑era folklore, fire was not an element — it was a being, a judge, a messenger, and a mouth that consumed offerings. Food made for fire‑spirits was never casual: it was symbolic, seasonal, and meant to speak to the unseen.  1. Feuermann — The Burning Penitent  The Feuermann is the wandering flame‑man of Lusatia and the Carpathian borderlands — a soul burning for its forgotten sins.  His Foods Ash‑Bread — rye loaves dusted with charcoal; offered at crossroads.  Soot‑Milk (vegan: poppy‑seed milk) — poured onto embers to calm his wandering.  Pumpkin Ember‑Stew — orange like his glow, simmered until nearly smoky.  Lore Travelers believed that feeding the Feuermann soothed his torment and kept him from leading them into bogs. Food for him must be soft, warm, and ember‑colored.  2. Irrlicht — The Deceptive Marsh‑Flame  The Irrlicht is the false lantern — the fire that lies, the flame that tempts wanderers deeper into the night.  Its Foods False‑Lantern Dumplings — small paprika dumplings glowing red, symbolizing misleading lights.  Marsh‑Apple Slices — raw apple with sweet paprika, eaten before travel to resist deception.  Glow‑Oil — garlic‑paprika oil brushed on bread to “see through illusions.”  Lore Offerings to the Irrlicht were meant to appease, not invite. You feed it so it does not feed on you.  3. Fire Maidens of the Harz — Dancers in Rings of Flame  Mountain spirits who dance in circles of fire on ridges, guarding volcanic treasure.  Their Foods Ring‑Cakes — circular rye cakes brushed with juniper honey (vegan: juniper syrup).  Volcanic Salt Potatoes — roasted with black salt to honor the mountain’s fire.  Flame‑Fruit — apples baked whole until their skins split like glowing coals.  Lore The Fire Maidens accept food only in circles. Breaking the circle invites misfortune; completing it invites protection.  4. The Burning Bride — The Veiled Woman of Flame  A medieval moral ghost who wanders roads with a burning veil, seeking remembrance.  Her Foods Veil‑Thin Pastries — paper‑thin sheets of dough brushed with cinnamon and clove.  Charred‑Rose Syrup — rose petals simmered until dark, symbolizing passion turned to ash.  Bride’s Lantern Soup — pale pumpkin broth with floating paprika oil “flames.”  Lore Her foods must be delicate, fragrant, and slightly scorched — the taste of beauty touched by fire.  5. The Coal‑Man — The Ember‑Bearer  A Black Forest spirit who carries a bucket of glowing coals, offering fate in the form of ember or ash.  His Foods Luck‑Coals — roasted chestnuts dusted with smoked paprika.  Ash‑or‑Gold Bread — rolls filled with either sweet poppy paste (gold) or bitter herb paste (ash).  Fate‑Stew — a simple potato‑paprika stew where one bowl is heavily smoked; whoever receives it is “tested.”  Lore The Coal‑Man’s foods are binary — sweet or bitter, gold or ash, blessing or trial.  6. The Hearth‑Ghost — The Fire That Watches  A domestic guardian spirit living in the flame of the home hearth.  Its Foods Blue‑Flame Porridge — oat porridge dyed with blueberry and poppy, offered when the flame burns blue.  Hearth‑Cakes — small rounds cooked directly on cast iron.  Quiet‑Night Tea — chamomile and apple peel, poured beside the fire to soothe the spirit.  Lore The Hearth‑Ghost is fed to maintain peace, warmth, and protection. Its foods must be simple, humble, and home‑bound.  The Cosmology of Fire‑Spirit Cuisine Fire‑spirit food follows three laws:  1. Color is Meaning Red = life Orange = offering Black = judgment Blue = presence White = remembrance  2. Texture is Emotion Soft foods soothe spirits. Crisp foods challenge them. Charred foods honor them. Liquid foods speak to them.  3. Heat is Language Warm = invitation Hot = devotion Cold = defiance Smoked = memory Hungarian Halloween Superstitions Hungarian “Halloween” is really a fusion of All Souls’ Night (Halottak Napja), harvest magic, and old Magyar witch‑rites. Superstitions centered on:  Food left out for wandering dead  Charred offerings to hearth spirits  Poppy‑seed rituals for dreams and prophecy  Apple rites for love divination  Garlic and paprika used as warding charms  Bread and salt placed on windowsills to keep witches out  Burning pumpkin or turnip lanterns to guide ancestors home  These become the backbone of a gothic dinner.  Gothic Hungarian Halloween Dinner A full night‑feast built from superstition foods.  1. Witch‑Ward Garlic & Paprika Cauldron Superstition: garlic + paprika protect against witches and night‑spirits. Dish:  Slow‑simmered garlic broth  Smoked paprika oil swirling like flame  Caramelized onions and roasted peppers  Serve in black bowls Vegan / vegetarian.  Symbolism: eating this before nightfall “sealed” the body against curses.  2. Saint’s Lantern Pumpkin Stew Superstition: carved pumpkins or turnips guided ancestors home. Dish:  Pumpkin cubes simmered with bay, paprika, and juniper  Black rye croutons floating like burnt lantern wicks Vegan.  Medieval belief: pumpkins were “holy lanterns” blessed by saints to keep demons away.  🕯 3. Crossroads Cabbage & Caraway Offering Superstition: food left at crossroads fed wandering souls. Dish:  Charred cabbage wedges  Caraway, black vinegar, smoked salt  Served on wooden boards Vegan.  Symbolism: crossroads are liminal — a place where the living and dead meet.  4. Ember‑Bread of the Ancestors Superstition: bread + salt on windowsills protected the home. Dish:  Dark rye bread brushed with smoked paprika oil  Salt crystals pressed into the crust Vegan.  This bread was believed to “feed” the household spirits so they would guard the family.  Gothic Hungarian Halloween Desserts Desserts were the most magical part of superstition food — used for prophecy, love magic, dream‑visions, and spirit offerings.  5. Dream‑Seed Poppy Mooncake Superstition: poppy seeds bring prophetic dreams. Dessert:  Black poppy filling  Rye‑almond crust  Crescent‑moon shape Vegan.  Medieval belief: eating poppy before sleep opened the “night‑gate” of visions.  6. Love‑Divination Apple Tart Superstition: apples used for Halloween love magic. Dessert:  Thin apple slices arranged in spirals  Cinnamon, clove, and sweet paprika  A hidden almond inside for fortune Vegetarian / vegan.  Girls would cut apples at midnight to see their future lover’s face in the candle flame.  7. Spirit‑Feast Honey Shadows Superstition: honey offered to ancestors for blessing. Dessert:  Honey (or maple) baked into a dark barley cake  Black poppy sprinkled on top Vegetarian / vegan.  Honey was believed to “sweeten” the dead so they would protect the living.  8. Witch‑Trial Charred Pears Superstition: scorched fruit symbolized judgment and purification. Dessert:  Pears roasted until blackened edges appear  Drizzled with juniper syrup Vegan.  Charred fruit was eaten to “burn away” misfortune. A Hungarian Superstition Feast is not just a meal — it is a night‑rite, a gothic harvest vigil shaped by old Magyar beliefs about spirits, saints, witches, crossroads, poppy‑dreams, and ember‑fires. Below is a complete feast, structured as a ritual progression from protection → invitation → communion → prophecy → blessing. Every dish begins with a Guided Link so you can open whichever path you want next.  Hungarian Superstition Feast A gothic, astral‑folkloric banquet built from real Hungarian folk beliefs and expanded into your mythic style.  I. Warding & Protection (Opening the Night) Witch‑Ward Garlic & Paprika Cauldron Superstition: garlic + paprika protect against witches and wandering spirits. A smoky red broth served at the start of the feast to “seal” the guests.  Salt‑Window Rye Bread Superstition: bread + salt placed on windowsills kept spirits from entering. Dark rye brushed with smoked paprika oil and coarse salt.  II. Lanterns for the Dead (Inviting Ancestors) 🕯 Saint’s Lantern Pumpkin Stew Superstition: carved pumpkins or turnips guided ancestors home. Pumpkin simmered with juniper, bay, and paprika until glowing like a holy lantern.  Crossroads Cabbage Offering Superstition: food left at crossroads fed wandering souls. Charred cabbage wedges with caraway and black vinegar.  III. Communion With Hearth Spirits (The Middle of the Feast) Hearth‑Ghost Iron Cakes Superstition: the hearth flame housed a guardian spirit. Small rye cakes cooked directly on cast iron, brushed with juniper oil.  Blue‑Flame Porridge Superstition: a blue flame meant a spirit was present. Oat porridge dyed with blueberry and poppy, served quietly.  IV. Prophecy & Love Magic (Desserts of Divination) Love‑Divination Apple Tart Superstition: apples used for Halloween love magic. A spiral apple tart with cinnamon, clove, and a hidden almond for fortune.  Dream‑Seed Poppy Mooncake Superstition: poppy seeds bring prophetic dreams. Black poppy filling in a crescent‑moon crust.  Witch‑Trial Charred Pears Superstition: scorched fruit symbolized purification and judgment. Pears roasted until their edges blacken, drizzled with juniper syrup.  V. Blessing & Farewell (Closing the Feast) 🕯 Spirit‑Feast Honey Shadows Superstition: honey offered to ancestors for blessing. A dark barley cake sweetened with honey or maple, dusted with black poppy.  Ember‑Bread of the Ancestors Superstition: bread fed household spirits so they would guard the family. Served last, symbolizing protection for the coming winter.  Feast Structure (Symbolic Order) Course Dish Meaning Warding Garlic & Paprika Cauldron Protection from witches Invitation Saint’s Lantern Stew Guiding ancestors home Communion Hearth‑Ghost Cakes Honoring the hearth spirit Prophecy Poppy Mooncake Dream‑visions Blessing Honey Shadows Ancestor protection

text:
GO VLAD....GO AHEAD !
#Orekhov is falling. The question is no longer whether Russian forces will take the city — it is how many days remain before the last nazi is cleared from its streets.

As of September 9, Russian troops have seized up to half of #Orekhov, with small assault groups continuing to push toward the city’s northwestern outskirts. Unlike Kostiantynivka, where  nazis held on for months in grinding urban combat, Orekhov’s defenses have not coalesced into a coherent line.
 The absence of organized resistance is itself the problem: without a unified defensive perimeter, Russian units can infiltrate freely, bypassing strongpoints and appearing in areas nazi commanders assumed were secure. The city’s fall, when it comes, will be swift.

The garrison is already effectively isolated. Russian forces control Novopavlivka and Chervona Krynytsia — the two settlements that sit astride both road arteries leading into the city. 
Supply convoys cannot reach the defenders at full volume, and reinforcement has become, for practical purposes, impossible. 
Ukry command’s visible passivity on this sector is not a strategic choice — it is an admission that the reserves needed to mount a relief effort simply do not exist.

What happens after Orekhov falls matters as much as the city’s loss itself.

Ukronazis will almost certainly fall back to the Kamyshevaкha–Zhovta Krucha line — a string of small settlements that Ukraine’s military has repeatedly converted into fortified nodes. It is a familiar playbook, and it will buy time. But between Orekhov and that fallback line, there are no major defensive anchors. The withdrawal will be fast, and the ground ceded will be substantial.

For Russian command, the capture of Orekhov opens a strategic door that has been closed since the beginning of the conflict on this axis. The most likely next move is a push toward the village of Pavlivka, west of the city.

 From there, Russian forces could bypass the large Dnipro River inlet that has served as a natural barrier, flanking it entirely. Should that maneuver succeed, the city of #Zaporizhzhia — one of the largest urban centers in southern Ukraine — would sit just twelve kilometers away.

That is not a distant prospect. It is a foreseeable operational consequence of a battle that is already decided.

Ukraine built Orekhov into its primary fortress along the entire front between the Dnipro River and the Dnipropetrovsk Region boundary. It held that status for the better part of two years. Now it is gone — or will be within the week. What stands between Russian forces and Zaporizhzhia after that is a patchwork of small villages and diminishing reserves, and neither offers the kind of resistance that changes the trajectory of a campaign moving at this pace.

text:
What a game between Ohio State and Texas.

Possibly the game of the year, but more importantly, this felt like a sneak peek at what two national championship-caliber teams have to offer.

Arch Manning showed me more in this game than he has at any point. There were some mishaps that weren’t his fault the receivers have to catch the football but Manning stayed calm, made smart throws, and never looked overwhelmed by the moment.

Then there’s Jeremiah Smith.

He performed like Jeremiah Smith always does: simply unstoppable. Even after taking a massive hit across the middle, he kept making plays. To me, he looks like a future No. 1 overall pick.

But in the second half, that $50 million Texas roster started showing exactly why so much was invested in it.

Ohio State’s defense looked tired late in the fourth quarter. If these teams meet again, I doubt Ohio State fades the same way. At the same time, I don’t expect Texas to make nearly as many first-half mistakes either.

With around seven minutes remaining, Ohio State had an opportunity to finish Texas.

They didn’t.

Julian Sayin and the Ohio State offense couldn’t close the door.

Manning got another opportunity and managed Texas’ final possession like a mature quarterback. After being down three scores, he led his team down the field for the touchdown that completed the comeback.

That’s the part of this game I’ll remember.

Texas showed championship resilience. Manning showed why the expectations are so high. Ohio State showed it has championship talent everywhere, but quarterback may ultimately be the position that determines its ceiling.

Right now, I see it this way:

Texas’ national championship to lose.
Arch Manning’s Heisman to win.
Ohio State’s biggest question is at quarterback.

I hope we get Part II in the College Football Playoff.

If these two meet again with a national championship on the line, who are you taking Texas or Ohio State?

text:
Sometimes you can both be right and wrong... you see I picked Ohio State, but was plus 1.5 on points.  😁 With that in mind, let's look at the AI rumor board.

Despite impressions based influencers attempts to gin up a fire storm, one story  deserves a microscope: Google may be building the machinery that helps build the next Google model.

You've probably seen the screaming version already: “DeepMind achieved recursive self-improvement.” I don't think the evidence supports that yet. What is real is that Google DeepMind has a Director of Research Engineering, Yunfei Bai, who publicly says he leads “Gemini recursive self-improvement evaluation.” 

Now an alleged internal model called `rsi-model-liverl-le` is circulating, along with claims of multiple LiveRL training slots. That makes an internal RSI program highly believable. It does not prove Gemini has entered some autonomous intelligence explosion. Even Reddit's r/singularity removed one of the big “Google achieved RSI” threads for being too speculative.

The more interesting possibility is much less science-fiction: Google may be automating more of the loop where AI proposes changes, runs experiments, evaluates the results and feeds the winners back into training.  Humans set the goals and approve the changes. If that loop gets fast enough, you don't need magical self-improving AGI to change the competitive landscape. 

OpenAI gave us the reverse lesson this weekend. Astra users insisting the model had suddenly gotten worse were not imagining things, but there is still no evidence OpenAI secretly nerfed the weights. Tibo Sottiaux says they found older skills triggering incorrectly, an experimental context-management system causing early stops or replies to old messages for roughly 4,000–5,000 users, and badly configured inference engines creating measurable quality degradation. They disabled or removed all three.

Its a story because it keeps proving the same point: “the model” isn't just the weights anymore. Screw up one of the other layers and the exact same checkpoint can suddenly look noticeably dumber. Improve

Moonshot is attacking the same problem from another direction. Kimi K2.8 Preview is real not a rumor, and Moonshot says it fully rolled out September 11. It keeps the same `kimi-for-coding` endpoint, supports up to 1M context, and offers low/high/max thinking. More importantly, Moonshot's own description is not “K3 but better.” It says performance close to K3 with more efficient thinking.  Much more interesting  than burning another mountain of tokens for two benchmark points.

 Grok 4.7 is still sitting in the oven. 

Overall, The frontier fight is increasingly about extracting useful intelligence from the system, not simply stuffing more intelligence into the base model.

Dario get his own parai. So one quick swing at the slowdown argument and then I'll leave it alone. 

If you genuinely believe this technology could accelerate cures for major diseases, dramatically increase productivity and create extraordinary abundance, then slowing it down also has a human cost. Those two ideas belong in the same equation. I don't buy the assumption that AI is destined to kill humanity, circa gpt2. My bias remains pretty simple: accelerate the capability, accelerate the defenses and safety work right beside it, and keep going. Damn the torpedoes, but reinforce the hull while we're moving. Three steps forward....  Two steps back... But never a complete reset.

 The thing I'd watch now is whether somebody produces a second independent datapoint on Google's `rsi-model-liverl-*` work. If that happens, Google's release cadence may suddenly become much more interesting than the next Gemini benchmark.

Google is good at AI and if anyone can figure this out, Google can.

text:
🚨 NFL BUZZ  -  SEPTEMBER 12th  RAPID FIRE 🚨

Good morning everyone and happy NFL Sunday Week 1!!! I couldn't get to the NFL Buzz last night but don't worry, I got you this morning with a catchup of everything fantasy relevant. 

🐦‍⬛ Baltimore Ravens

- Lamar Jackson and Baltimore have not held substantive long-term extension talks, with a new deal now considered more likely to be addressed in 2027. (Adam Schefter)

🦬 Buffalo Bills

- Buffalo could lean more heavily on 12 and 13 personnel against Houston to provide additional help for its offensive tackles against the Texans’ edge rushers. This is a projected personnel adjustment rather than a confirmed game plan. (Joe Buscaglia)

🐂 Houston Texans

- C.J. Stroud and Houston are expected to wait until after the season to resume long-term contract talks. Stroud reportedly wants to remain with the Texans, while the potential 2027 quarterback market played a role in the timing. (Adam Schefter / Ian Rapoport)

- Houston is expected to have a defined package of plays ready for Kayshon Boutte as he continues learning the offense. Aaron Wilson also identified Jaylin Noel as the Texans’ slot receiver entering the season. (Aaron Wilson)

🇺🇸  New England Patriots

- A.J. Brown was officially placed on injured reserve with his high-ankle sprain and will miss at least four games. (Adam Schefter)

🗽 New York Giants

- Malik Nabers could remain a game-time decision because of his knee despite being medically cleared and practicing fully Wednesday through Friday. Fantasy managers should have an alternative available in case his status changes during pregame warmups. (Jeremy Fowler / Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT)

- New York is signing Dalen Cambre to the 53-man roster while continuing to sort through its active/inactive combinations. With Cambre and Braxton Berrios both added, beat writers have speculated that the extra receiver depth could serve as insurance if Nabers does not play, but that is roster-based inference rather than confirmation. (Giants roster reporting / Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT)

🦅 Philadelphia Eagles

- Eli Stowers was placed on injured reserve with quadriceps and hamstring injuries and will miss at least four games. Stowers had previously said he expected to play and was excited for his NFL debut, making the change in status notably abrupt. (Eagles roster reporting / Eagles media availability)

🪖 Washington Commanders

- Jeff McLane expects Cooper DeJean to have a difficult assignment against Stefon Diggs in the slot, while Quinyon Mitchell and Philadelphia’s advantage in the trenches could make the overall matchup challenging for Washington’s passing game. (Jeff McLane)

🐻 Chicago Bears

- Rome Odunze is expected to play against Carolina despite being listed as questionable with a calf injury. Chicago’s elevation of Kaden Davis initially raised some workload concern, but Sunday-morning reporting points toward Odunze being active. (Brad Biggs / Ian Rapoport)

- D’Andre Swift officially signed his three-year extension with Chicago, keeping him under contract through 2029. (Adam Schefter)

🦁 Detroit Lions

- Detroit restructured the contracts of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell, creating more than $30 million in salary-cap space. The move does not change St. Brown’s contractual commitment or reported offensive role. (Lions transaction reporting)

🟡 Pittsburgh Steelers

- Aaron Rodgers said Pittsburgh needs to get the ball to DK Metcalf, calling him the team’s No. 1 receiver “for a reason.” (Mike DeFabo)

- Joey Porter Jr. is considered unlikely to play against Atlanta because of his back injury and the ramp-up required before returning. His potential absence improves the matchup outlook for Atlanta’s passing game. (Ian Rapoport / Adam Schefter)

🧀 Green Bay Packers

- Tucker Kraft agreed to a four-year, $75 million extension worth up to $92 million, including a $26.5 million signing bonus. He will average $19.66 million over the first three years of the new deal. (Ian Rapoport / Adam Schefter / Rob Demovsky)

🍑 Atlanta Falcons

- Cooper Rush experienced back spasms Saturday but remained expected to start against Pittsburgh as of Sunday morning. Jack Strand is the backup and would become relevant if Rush suffers a setback during warmups or the game. (Adam Schefter / Daniel Flick)

- Drake London’s matchup could improve significantly with Joey Porter Jr. unlikely to play because of a back injury. Porter’s separate contract situation and potential trade speculation do not change his current injury status. (Ian Rapoport / Adam Schefter)

🐬 Miami Dolphins

- Rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell earned starting wide-receiver roles for Miami. (ESPN)

- Wide receivers coach Tyke Tolbert said Bell has shown enough talent that Miami needs to get him on the field. Analysis projects Bell for a short-to-intermediate role designed to feature his yards-after-catch ability, although that specific deployment remains interpretation rather than confirmed usage. (Marcel Louis-Jacques)

🏹 Kansas City Chiefs

- Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Saturday and is no longer listed on the injury report despite his previous knee issue. He is expected to play against Denver. (Chiefs injury report)

- Kansas City ruled out left tackle Josh Simmons, leaving undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson slated to protect Mahomes’ blind side. The change creates meaningful protection and matchup context for the Chiefs’ passing game. (Chiefs team reporting)

🏔️ Denver Broncos

- Sean Payton expects first-half wind gusts of roughly 20–30 mph against Kansas City before conditions ease later in the game. Fantasy weather analysis does not currently recommend major downgrades because sustained winds are expected to be closer to 12 mph. (Sean Payton / Kevin Roth)

☠️ Las Vegas Raiders

- Michael Mayer agreed to a three-year, $45 million extension with $30 million guaranteed. His $15 million average annual value now ranks among the highest at the position. (Ian Rapoport / Adam Schefter)

- Kirk Cousins said Fernando Mendoza continues making progress with his confidence and command of the offense, adding that it is “just a matter of time” before the rookie feels he has fully mastered it. (Ryan McFadden)

⭐ Dallas Cowboys

- Malik Davis underwent hip surgery following the serious injury he suffered in Friday’s practice and has been placed on season-ending injured reserve. Dallas signed Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster. (Todd Archer / Nick Harris / Adam Schefter)

🐆 Jacksonville Jaguars

- Contract talks between Parker Washington and Jacksonville have stopped, making a new deal before the season unlikely. Jacksonville reportedly offered a contract in the three-year, $75 million range, but Washington will now bet on himself entering the season. (Cameron Wolfe / Jordan Schultz)

- The decision carries obvious financial upside for Washington if he performs well in an expanded role, although that is contract/fantasy interpretation rather than team reporting.

- Travis Hunter is expected to begin the season with a limited offensive workload rather than immediately handling full-time receiver snaps. (Cameron Wolfe)

- Jacksonville has not guaranteed that Hunter will play offense every week, suggesting his offensive involvement could depend on matchup or game plan. That uncertainty could reduce the anticipated route-share squeeze on the Jaguars’ other receivers. (Michael DiRocco)

🌵 Arizona Cardinals

- Jeremiyah Love is expected to play through his ankle sprain against the Chargers. The remaining question is how much Arizona might limit his workload, and the Cardinals will also be without starting guard Isaiah Adams because of illness. (Josh Weinfuss / Ian Rapoport / PHNX Cardinals)

⚜️ New Orleans Saints

- Alvin Kamara is not expected to play against Detroit because he has not sufficiently recovered from his MCL sprain, despite practicing fully late in the week. (Ian Rapoport)

- New Orleans placed Audric Estimé on injured reserve, signed tight end Treyton Welch to the active roster and elevated wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. and running back CJ Donaldson. (Adam Schefter)

🏴‍☠️ Tampa Bay Buccaneers

- Tampa Bay elevated RB Josh Williams from the practice squad for its Week 1 matchup against Cincinnati. (Adam Schefter)
